aichi:sawada_shuzo.tagline_en: A Tokoname sake house whose junmai-ginjo umeshu took silver at the 2024 National Umeshu Awards.
aichi:sawada_shuzo.desc_en: Sawada Shuzo, a sake brewery in Tokoname, Aichi, makes plum liqueurs on a junmai ginjo sake base. Its Chita Hakurobai umeshu won silver in the sake-based division of the 2024 National Umeshu Awards, and UMESHU T ("Tsunagu") took silver in the premium division.
features_en: Two silver medals at the 2024 National Umeshu Awards
Umeshu built on junmai ginjo sake

知多 白老梅 純米吟醸仕込の梅酒.specs_en: Junmai ginjo base — silver, 2024 National Umeshu Awards

UMESHU T ～つなぐ～.specs_en: Silver, premium division, 2024 National Umeshu Awards

aichi:nakano_shuzo.tagline_en: The Kunizakari brewers of Handa, pressing real fruit into more than ten additive-free liqueurs.
aichi:nakano_shuzo.desc_en: Nakano Shuzo, founded in 1844 on the Chita Peninsula, brews the local sake Kunizakari and makes the Fruria line of high-juice fruit liqueurs — more than ten kinds including mikan orange (80% juice), peach, strawberry, grape and apple, all made without added flavourings or acidifiers. Its sake culture museum, Kunizakari Sake no Bunkakan, is open to visitors.

國盛 フルリア みかんのお酒.specs_en: 80% Japanese mikan juice, no added flavourings

akita:dewatsuru.tagline_en: White Kaga plums steeped in junmai sake brewed from Akitakomachi rice.
akita:dewatsuru.desc_en: Founded in 1865, Akita Seishu brews Dewatsuru Umegokochi, a plum liqueur of Shirakaga plums steeped in junmai sake made from Akitakomachi rice. It carries a fresh, peach-like aroma at 11% ABV.
features_en: Junmai sake base brewed from Akitakomachi rice

出羽鶴 梅ごこち.specs_en: Junmai sake base, Shirakaga plums — 11% ABV

akita:hinomaru_jozo.tagline_en: A 1689 Yokote brewery pouring its sake craft into a cheesecake-rich yogurt liqueur.
akita:hinomaru_jozo.desc_en: Hinomaru Jozo, founded in 1689 in Yokote, Akita, keeps a storehouse registered as a National Tangible Cultural Property and brews more than sixty sakes. That range of technique feeds its Yogurushu — a yogurt liqueur with a dense, cheesecake-like richness under the Mansaku no Hana label.

aomori:hatomasamune.tagline_en: Umeshu and a snow-cloudy apple liqueur from the underground waters of Hakkoda.
aomori:hatomasamune.desc_en: Hatomasamune, founded in 1899 in Towada, Aomori, brews with subsoil water from the Hakkoda and Oirase watershed. It makes the Hachitsuru Nmē Umeshu plum liqueur and the popular Yuki Ringo, which blends Aomori apple juice with cloudy nigori sake.

雪りんご.specs_en: Aomori apple juice blended with nigori sake

aomori:momokawa.tagline_en: One of Aomori's flagship breweries, turning local apples and cassis into liqueur.
aomori:momokawa.desc_en: Momokawa, founded in 1889 in Oirase, is one of Aomori's leading sake houses. Its apple liqueur Ringo ni Koishita Osake, made with Aomori apples, has won the A-1 Grand Prix and the chairman's prize at the Aomori Furusato Food Contest; an Aomori cassis liqueur made from 100% local cassis, free of flavourings and colourings, completes the line.

りんごに恋したお酒.name_en: Ringo ni Koishita Osake (In Love with Apples)
りんごに恋したお酒.specs_en: Aomori apples — A-1 Grand Prix winner

あおもりカシス.specs_en: 100% Aomori cassis, no flavourings or colourings

chiba:iinuma_honke.tagline_en: Chiba plums resting in Kinoene Masamune sake, from a 300-year house.
chiba:iinuma_honke.desc_en: Iinuma Honke, a Chiba sake brewery with over three centuries of history, steeps fine local plums in its Kinoene Masamune sake to make Umekichi — a clean, gently sweet and easy-drinking umeshu at 11% ABV.
features_en: Over 300 years of brewing in Chiba

chiba:koizumi_shuzo.tagline_en: A Futtsu brewery whose Tokai umeshu medalled at the 2024 National Umeshu Awards.
chiba:koizumi_shuzo.desc_en: Koizumi Shuzo, a sake brewery in Futtsu, Chiba, makes Tokai Umeshu, which won silver in the mixed-base division of the 2024 National Umeshu Awards.
features_en: Silver, mixed-base division, 2024 National Umeshu Awards

ehime:eikoo.tagline_en: Additive-free umeshu of Ehime Nanko plums on honkaku shochu, from a gold-medal sake house.
ehime:eikoo.desc_en: Eiko Shuzo of Matsuyama, a brewery with gold medals from the Annual Japan Sake Awards, steeps Ehime-grown Nanko plums in honkaku (single-distilled) shochu with no acidifiers, colourings or flavourings — a crisp umeshu with restrained sweetness. The house also makes mikan liqueurs from Ehime citrus.

蔵元の梅酒.specs_en: Honkaku shochu base, Ehime Nanko plums, additive-free

蔵元のみかん.specs_en: Ehime ponkan juice, shochu base — gold, Matsuyama Brand New Product Contest 2022

ehime:umenishiki.tagline_en: Umeshu from a storied Ehime brewery with more than thirty national gold medals.
ehime:umenishiki.desc_en: Umenishiki Yamakawa, the celebrated Ehime brewer of Umenishiki sake with more than thirty gold medals at the Annual Japan Sake Awards, makes a sake-based plum liqueur under the same name.
features_en: 30+ gold medals at the Annual Japan Sake Awards

ehime:kondo_shuzo.tagline_en: Niihama's last remaining brewery, generous with Ehime mandarins.
ehime:kondo_shuzo.desc_en: Kondo Shuzo, founded in 1878, is the last brewery remaining in Niihama, Ehime. The fifth-generation head became toji (master brewer) in 2001 and restarted in-house brewing; its Ehime Mikan de Sake liqueur is loaded with Ehime-grown satsuma mandarins.

fukui:ippongi.tagline_en: Fukui plums in a four-to-one blend of sake and shochu, sweet like fine honey.
fukui:ippongi.desc_en: Ippongi Kubo Honten of Katsuyama, Fukui, makes Ippongi Ume no Utage entirely from Fukui-grown plums, steeped in a blend of 80% sake and 20% shochu. The result carries a deep, honeyed sweetness balanced by fresh plum acidity.

fukuoka:shinozaki.tagline_en: An Edo-period Chikuzen house whose Amaou-strawberry umeshu keeps winning at Tenma Tenjin.
fukuoka:shinozaki.desc_en: Shinozaki was founded in the late Edo period in what is now Asakura, Fukuoka, and makes sake, shochu, amazake and liqueurs. Its Amaou strawberry umeshu, "Amaou, Hajimemashita.", has placed at the Tenma Tenjin Umeshu Festival two years running, and the house holds a Monde Selection Grand Gold among its honours.
features_en: Amaou strawberry umeshu — two straight years of Tenma Tenjin honours

fukuoka:nishiyoshida.tagline_en: The Tsukushi barley-shochu makers, gold medallists for their 17-degree umeshu.
fukuoka:nishiyoshida.desc_en: Nishiyoshida Shuzo of Chikugo, Fukuoka, is known for its honkaku barley shochu Tsukushi. Its Tsukushi Umeshu 17 won gold in the honkaku-shochu division of the 2024 National Umeshu Awards.
features_en: Umeshu from the Tsukushi barley-shochu house
Gold, honkaku-shochu division, 2024 National Umeshu Awards

つくし梅酒 17度.specs_en: Honkaku shochu base — 17% ABV, gold at the 2024 National Umeshu Awards

fukuoka:oga_shuzo.tagline_en: Fukuoka's oldest brewery (1673), steeping plums in sake made with Homanzan spring water.
fukuoka:oga_shuzo.desc_en: Oga Shuzo, founded in 1673, is the oldest sake brewery in Fukuoka Prefecture, committed to handwork and brewing with the subsoil water of Mt. Homan. Its Tamadeizumi Umeshu won silver in the sake-based division of the 2024 National Umeshu Awards.
features_en: Silver, sake-based division, 2024 National Umeshu Awards

玉出泉 梅酒.specs_en: Sake base — silver, 2024 National Umeshu Awards

fukuoka:wakanami_shuzo.tagline_en: Qdamon — Kyushu dialect for "fruit" — a strawberry liqueur of Hakata Amaou on the Chikugo riverbank.
fukuoka:wakanami_shuzo.desc_en: Wakanami Shuzo, founded in 1922 on the banks of the Chikugo River in Okawa, Fukuoka, makes the Qdamon line of Kyushu fruit liqueurs — the name means "fruit" in Kyushu dialect. Its Hakata Amaou strawberry liqueur, at a gentle 5% ABV, is the flagship.

fukushima:daishichi.tagline_en: Kimoto umeshu — Kishu Nanko plums in Daishichi's junmai kimoto genshu.
fukushima:daishichi.desc_en: Daishichi, founded in 1752 in Nihonmatsu, has kept to traditional kimoto brewing for over 250 years. Its Kimoto Umeshu steeps Kishu Nanko plums in undiluted junmai kimoto sake and holds a gold medal from the Féminalise wine competition; a long-aged Gokujo Umeshu completes the pair.

大七 生もと梅酒.specs_en: Junmai kimoto genshu base, Kishu Nanko plums — 12% ABV

fukushima:akebono_shuzo.tagline_en: Snowdrop — an Aizu collaboration of local yogurt, local rice and sake.
fukushima:akebono_shuzo.desc_en: Akebono Shuzo, founded in 1904 in Aizubange, makes the sake-based yogurt liqueur Snowdrop with Aizu Chuo Dairy — Aizu raw-milk yogurt and Mizuho Kogane rice grown in Aizubange. Gentle at 5% ABV, it is a favourite with newcomers to sake.

gifu:hirata_shuzojo.tagline_en: Takayama's Umegoyomi, a silver medallist at the 2024 National Umeshu Awards.
gifu:hirata_shuzojo.desc_en: Hirata Shuzojo, a sake house in Takayama, Gifu, makes Umegoyomi, which won silver in the mixed-base division of the 2024 National Umeshu Awards.
features_en: Silver, mixed-base division, 2024 National Umeshu Awards

gifu:nakashima_jozo.tagline_en: Kozaemon yuzu-shu: Umaji Village yuzu, nothing less than 100% of it.
gifu:nakashima_jozo.desc_en: Nakashima Jozo, founded in 1702 in Mizunami, Gifu, makes Kozaemon Yuzushu with 100% yuzu juice from Umaji Village in Kochi — the fruit's most celebrated source — on a sake base.

gunma:hijiri_shuzo.tagline_en: A Shibukawa brewery since 1841, ranging from umeshu to blood orange.
gunma:hijiri_shuzo.desc_en: Hijiri Shuzo, founded in 1841 in Shibukawa, Gunma, keeps its traditional sake craft while making a spread of liqueurs — umeshu, yuzu and a blood-orange liqueur among them.

gunma:kondo_shuzo_gunma.tagline_en: Shu Shu Shu Shu — Gunma fruit set into a dry house's junmai ginjo.
gunma:kondo_shuzo_gunma.desc_en: Kondo Shuzo, founded in 1875 and brewing dry sake with the subsoil water of Mt. Akagi, makes the Shu Shu Shu Shu liqueur series: junmai ginjo sake married with Gunma-grown plum, yuzu and blueberry.
features_en: Founded 1875 at the foot of Mt. Akagi
Junmai ginjo base with Gunma-grown fruit

hiroshima:kamotsuru.tagline_en: Saijo's great name, whose junmai umeshu entered the National Umeshu Awards hall of fame.
hiroshima:kamotsuru.desc_en: Kamotsuru, the celebrated Saijo brewery founded in 1873, makes its umeshu from just three things: junmai sake, fully ripened Kishu Nanko plums and rock sugar. It won gold and first place three years running at the National Umeshu Awards — earning hall-of-fame status — and a version steeped in junmai ginjo sake aged over ten years extends the line.
features_en: Hall of fame — three straight National Umeshu Awards golds
Junmai sake, Nanko plums, rock sugar — nothing else

賀茂鶴 純米酒仕込 梅酒.specs_en: Junmai base, ripe Kishu Nanko plums — National Umeshu Awards hall of fame

hiroshima:sakurao_bd.tagline_en: A 1918 Hiroshima house ageing its umeshu in whisky casks.
hiroshima:sakurao_bd.desc_en: Founded in 1918 as Chugoku Jozo and renamed Sakurao Brewery and Distillery in 2021, this Hatsukaichi maker spans sake, shochu, mirin, liqueurs, gin and whisky. Its liqueurs lean individual: a whisky-cask-aged SAKURAO umeshu, a GABA-enriched umeshu and a red-shiso liqueur from Hiroshima leaves.
features_en: Gin and whisky under the same roof

hokkaido:takasago_hokkaido.tagline_en: Asahikawa's Kokushimuso umeshu, blended in the LAB with Hokkaido fruit.
hokkaido:takasago_hokkaido.desc_en: Takasago Shuzo, founded in 1899 in Asahikawa, brews with subsoil water of the Daisetsuzan range and Hokkaido-grown sake rice. Its sake-based Kokushimuso Umeshu anchors the Ezokura Umeshu LAB. series, which blends in fruit from around Hokkaido, such as Furano grapes.

hyogo:hakutsuru.tagline_en: Nada's Hakutsuru, squeezing whole fruit into its Marugoto Shibori line.
hyogo:hakutsuru.desc_en: Hakutsuru, the Nada Gogo house founded in 1743, makes the Marugoto Shibori ("whole-pressed") liqueur line — yuzu, peach and lemon pressed whole — plus the jelly-textured Purupuru series. The Hakutsuru Sake Brewery Museum in Kobe opens its brewing culture to visitors.

hyogo:kikumasamune.tagline_en: The kimoto masters of Nada, turning their hand to umeshu.
hyogo:kikumasamune.desc_en: Kiku-Masamune, founded in 1659 and famed for kimoto-method sake, makes a sake-based umeshu and fruit liqueurs from its Nada home in Kobe.

hyogo:ozeki.tagline_en: Three centuries of Nishinomiya brewing behind an easy-going umeshu.
hyogo:ozeki.desc_en: Ozeki, founded in 1711 in Nishinomiya and known worldwide for its One Cup sake, extends more than 300 years of brewing into plum and fruit liqueurs.

hyogo:sawanotsuru.tagline_en: Umeshu built on aged sake — gold at the 2024 National Umeshu Awards.
hyogo:sawanotsuru.desc_en: Sawanotsuru, the junmai-minded Nada brewery founded in 1717, makes Koshu Jikomi Umeshu on a base of aged sake. It took gold in the sake-based division of the 2024 National Umeshu Awards.

沢の鶴 古酒仕込み梅酒.specs_en: Aged-sake base, Kishu Nanko plums — gold, 2024

hyogo:nishiyama_shuzojo.tagline_en: Baishin Shunju — ripe-plum purée nigori umeshu from the Kotsuzumi house of Tamba.
hyogo:nishiyama_shuzojo.desc_en: Nishiyama Shuzojo, the Tamba brewery founded in 1849 and home of Kotsuzumi sake, makes Baishin Shunju, a cloudy umeshu enriched with ripe plum purée. It won gold in the nigori division of the 2024 National Umeshu Awards.
features_en: Gold, nigori division, 2024 National Umeshu Awards

梅申春秋.specs_en: Nigori umeshu with ripe plum purée — gold, 2024

hyogo:houmei.tagline_en: Tamba-Sasayama umeshu on a sake base, silver medallist in 2024.
hyogo:houmei.desc_en: Houmei Shuzo of Tamba-Sasayama makes a sake-based umeshu that won silver in the sake-based division of the 2024 National Umeshu Awards.

ibaraki:meiri.tagline_en: Hyakunen Umeshu — the brandy-steeped umeshu once crowned best in Japan, from Mito's plum country.
ibaraki:meiri.desc_en: Meiri Shurui, founded in 1950 near Mito's famous Kairakuen plum garden, steeps domestic plums in brandy — an unusual base that carried its Baiko Hyakunen Umeshu to first place in Japan at the National Umeshu Awards. A long-aged premium version follows at 17% ABV.
features_en: Best in Japan at the National Umeshu Awards

ishikawa:kobori.tagline_en: Kaga Umeshu, Ishikawa's favourite, from the 300-year Manzairaku house.
ishikawa:kobori.desc_en: Kobori Shuzoten of Tsurugi, Hakusan, has brewed the famed Manzairaku sake for more than three centuries. Its Kaga Umeshu is the most popular plum liqueur in Ishikawa Prefecture.

iwate:nanbubijin.tagline_en: Sugar-free umeshu — all-koji junmai sake and Iwate plums, nothing added.
iwate:nanbubijin.desc_en: Nanbu Bijin, founded in 1902 in Ninohe, is known for its sugar-free umeshu: all-koji junmai sake and Iwate-grown plums alone, letting the rice's umami and the fruit's aroma carry the drink at 9–10% ABV. The brewery holds kosher certification. A mountain-grape blend widens the range.

南部美人 糖類無添加梅酒.specs_en: All-koji junmai base, no added sugar — 9–10% ABV

iwate:asabiraki.tagline_en: Umekanon — junmai-based umeshu on one of Japan's hundred famous waters.
iwate:asabiraki.desc_en: Asabiraki, the leading Morioka brewery founded in 1871, brews with Daiji Shimizu, one of the Heisei-era Hundred Famous Waters. Its junmai-based Umekanon umeshu heads a line of Japanese-style liqueurs.

kagawa:nishino_kinryo.tagline_en: The shrine brewers of Konpira-san, with 230 years behind their umeshu.
kagawa:nishino_kinryo.desc_en: Nishino Kinryo, with over 230 years of history in Kotohira, Kagawa, brews the sacred sake of the Konpira shrine and the Kinryo sake line, alongside umeshu and other liqueurs. It is also known for sake made with Setouchi olive yeast.

kagoshima:komasa.tagline_en: Organic plums and honey in honkaku shochu, from a Meiji-era Kagoshima house.
kagoshima:komasa.desc_en: Komasa Jozo, a Kagoshima shochu house dating to the Meiji era, makes its umeshu with organically grown plums from the Takasudo farm in Nara and honey, on a honkaku shochu base, free of flavourings and colourings — 14% ABV.

小正の梅酒 本格焼酎仕込み.specs_en: Honkaku shochu base, organic plums and honey — 14% ABV

kagoshima:hamada_shuzo.tagline_en: The Kaido and Daimao makers' smooth-mouthed umeshu, with a gold-mine cellar edition.
kagoshima:hamada_shuzo.desc_en: Hamada Shuzo, founded in 1868 in Ichikikushikino and known for the imo (sweet-potato) shochus Kaido and Daimao, makes Kuchimaro Umeshu at 14% ABV and a long-aged umeshu sold only at its Kinzangura, a cellar set in a former gold mine.

kagoshima:yamamoto_shuzo_kagoshima.tagline_en: Godai umeshu on imo shochu, with the cloudy Umeta alongside.
kagoshima:yamamoto_shuzo_kagoshima.desc_en: Yamamoto Shuzo, a Kagoshima shochu house in Satsumasendai, makes Godai Umeshu on an imo (sweet-potato) shochu base and the popular cloudy umeshu Umeta.

kagoshima:shiratama_jozo.tagline_en: From the house of Maoh — the Satsuma umeshu, Saiko.
kagoshima:shiratama_jozo.desc_en: Shiratama Jozo of Kinko, Kagoshima, famed for the imo shochu Maoh, makes Saiko no Umeshu — the Satsuma umeshu — at 14% ABV.

kagoshima:hombo_shuzo.tagline_en: Joto Umeshu from the Hoshigura — additive-free, Kura Master platinum.
kagoshima:hombo_shuzo.desc_en: Hombo Shuzo, the Kagoshima drinks house founded in 1872, steeps fresh green plums each June at its Hoshigura cellar — Nanko, large-fruit and Shirakaga varieties — into Joto Umeshu, made without flavourings, colourings or acidifiers. It took platinum at Kura Master 2023 and gold in 2024; a Chiran-tea version follows at 10% ABV.

kanagawa:izumibashi.tagline_en: Yamada Juro — a rice-farming brewery's umeshu of Odawara's famed Juro plums.
kanagawa:izumibashi.desc_en: Izumibashi, founded in 1857 in Ebina, grows its own rice and brews from grain to glass. Its umeshu, Yamada Juro, steeps Juro plums from Soga in Odawara in junmai sake; a strawberry liqueur made with locally grown Ebina Tochiotome berries joins the line.
features_en: Odawara Soga Juro plums in junmai sake

kanagawa:kumazawa.tagline_en: Shonan's only brewery — sake, beer and liqueur by the coast.
kanagawa:kumazawa.desc_en: Kumazawa Shuzo, founded in 1872 in Chigasaki, is the only brewery on the Shonan coast, making Tensei sake, craft beer and a line of liqueurs.

kanagawa:dover.tagline_en: The bartender's Japanese pantry — twelve Wa-shu liqueurs from sakura to matcha.
kanagawa:dover.desc_en: Dover Shuzo of Atsugi is a specialist in liqueurs for bars and patisserie. Its Wa-shu series runs to twelve Japanese botanicals — sakura, matcha, yuzu, ume and mugwort among them — and enjoys strong support from professional bartenders.
features_en: Specialist bar and patisserie liqueur maker

kochi:tsukasabotan.tagline_en: Wild mountain yuzu, junmai sake and sugar — nothing else — from a 1603 Tosa house.
kochi:tsukasabotan.desc_en: Tsukasabotan, founded in 1603 in Sakawa, Kochi, makes Yama-yuzu Shibori from pesticide-free mountain yuzu of the Tosa Reihoku highlands, junmai sake and sugar alone — no flavourings, colourings, acidifiers or preservatives, at a soft 8% ABV. French chefs received it warmly at a Paris tasting.
features_en: Praised by French chefs in Paris

司牡丹 山柚子搾り ゆずの酒.specs_en: Junmai base, Reihoku mountain yuzu — 8% ABV, additive-free

kochi:kikusui_kochi.tagline_en: Aki's Edo-founded brewery, coarse-pressing Tosa yuzu into liqueur.
kochi:kikusui_kochi.desc_en: Kikusui Shuzo of Aki, Kochi, founded in the Edo period, makes Aragoshi Yuzu — a coarsely pressed liqueur of Kochi yuzu with a bright aroma and clean finish.

kochi:umaji_mura.tagline_en: The yuzu village itself — Umaji's co-op liqueur of yuzu and honey, nothing artificial.
kochi:umaji_mura.desc_en: The agricultural cooperative of Umaji Village — Japan's most famous yuzu village — makes its liqueur from yuzu and honey with no flavourings or sweeteners, keeping the fruit's natural aroma, acidity and sweetness.
features_en: Yuzu and honey only — no flavourings or sweeteners

kochi:tosatsuru.tagline_en: Kochi's flagship sake house, with a yuzu liqueur to match.
kochi:tosatsuru.desc_en: Tosatsuru, one of Kochi's flagship sake breweries, makes a sake-based liqueur of Kochi yuzu.

kumamoto:zuiyo.tagline_en: Kumamoto plums finished in junmai sake by the house of Toyo red sake.
kumamoto:zuiyo.desc_en: Zuiyo, founded in 1867 and known for the ceremonial red sake Toyo, steeps Kumamoto-grown plums in its own shochu and finishes the umeshu with junmai sake — 15% ABV.
features_en: Kumamoto plums, shochu and junmai sake

瑞鷹 梅酒 純米酒仕立て.specs_en: Shochu and junmai sake base, Kumamoto plums — 15% ABV

kumamoto:chiyonosono.tagline_en: Amanatsu, cherry and a plum liqueur built on 400-year-old red sake.
kumamoto:chiyonosono.desc_en: Chiyonosono, founded in 1896 in Yamaga, Kumamoto, makes sake, red sake, shochu and liqueurs. Its trio of fruit liqueurs — amanatsu citrus, cherry and Ume Akazake — is popular, the last steeped in akazake, the red sake with 400 years of history in Kumamoto.

千代の園 梅赤酒.specs_en: Red-sake base with 400 years of history

kyoto:gekkeikan.tagline_en: Fushimi's 1637 institution, easing sake drinkers into fruit with Horodoke.
kyoto:gekkeikan.desc_en: Gekkeikan, founded in 1637 in Fushimi, extends its sake into a fruit liqueur line: sake-based umeshu and yuzushu, and the low-alcohol Horodoke series — peach at 3% and strawberry at 3.5% ABV with Japanese fruit juice. The Gekkeikan Okura Sake Museum welcomes visitors.

kyoto:takara_shuzo.tagline_en: Takara's Sanchi Meguri — a tour of Japan's orchards, one liqueur at a time.
kyoto:takara_shuzo.desc_en: Takara Shuzo, the Fushimi drinks maker with history back to 1842 and Japan's largest name in shochu and mirin, makes a Sho Chiku Bai umeshu of 100% Japanese Nanko plums at 10% ABV, and the Sanchi Meguri series that bottles regional fruit — Miyazaki mango, Furano melon, Yamanashi peach and mikan among them.

kyoto:kizakura.tagline_en: Kyoto plums from Aotani, thickened to a nigori in Fushimi sake.
kyoto:kizakura.desc_en: Kizakura, founded in 1926 in Fushimi, processes white plums from Aotani — Kyoto's plum heartland — in-house and steeps them in Fushimi sake for Kyo-bijin Torori Umeshu, a cloudy style rounded with ripe plum purée.
features_en: Kyoto Aotani plums in Fushimi sake

京美人 京都でうまれたとろり梅酒.specs_en: Sake base, Kyoto Aotani plums, cloudy

mie:hayakawa_shuzo.tagline_en: Tenka Shunbai — plum liqueur from a 1915 Komono brewery.
mie:hayakawa_shuzo.desc_en: Hayakawa Shuzo, founded in 1915 in Komono, Mie, makes the plum liqueur Tenka Shunbai.

mie:ota_shuzo.tagline_en: Hanzo's umeshu — Minabe plums hand-steeped in the G7 summit toast sake's genshu.
mie:ota_shuzo.desc_en: Ota Shuzo, founded in 1892 in Iga, brews Hanzo, the sake served for the toast at the Ise-Shima Summit. Since 2007 it has steeped Nanko plums from Minabe by hand in undiluted sake brewed from Mie rice and Suzuka Mountains subsoil water — aged three years for its umeshu.
features_en: Brewer of the Ise-Shima Summit toast sake

半蔵の梅酒.specs_en: Three-year-aged sake base, Minabe Nanko plums

miyagi:nakayu_shuzoten.tagline_en: A double-gold yuzu umeshu from a hand-crafting Kami brewery.
miyagi:nakayu_shuzoten.desc_en: Nakayu Shuzoten, a traditional hand-crafting sake brewery in Kami, Miyagi, took a double gold at the 2024 National Umeshu Awards — in both the citrus-blend and brandy-blend divisions — with its Tenjo Mugen "Date na Yuzu Umeshu".
features_en: Double gold at the 2024 National Umeshu Awards

天上夢幻 蔵人仕込みの伊達なゆず梅酒.name_en: Tenjo Mugen Date na Yuzu Umeshu
天上夢幻 蔵人仕込みの伊達なゆず梅酒.specs_en: Double gold (citrus-blend and brandy-blend), 2024 National Umeshu Awards

miyagi:kanbai_shuzo.tagline_en: Hi no Shizuku — Yamamoto strawberries in sake from a grow-your-own-rice house.
miyagi:kanbai_shuzo.desc_en: Kanbai Shuzo, founded in 1918 and the only Miyagi brewery to run the full cycle from rice growing to brewing, makes Hi no Shizuku — a strawberry liqueur of 100% Yamamoto-grown fruit juice on a sake base at 6% ABV.

陽のしずく いちご酒.specs_en: Sake base, 100% Yamamoto strawberry juice — 6% ABV

miyagi:niizawa_jozo.tagline_en: Ultra-rich yogurt liqueur from the Hakurakusei brewers — Jersey milk, kept cold, gone fast.
miyagi:niizawa_jozo.desc_en: Niizawa Jozo, founded in 1873 and the house behind Hakurakusei and Atagonomatsu, blends 100% Jersey-milk yogurt with sake for its Cho-Noko ("ultra-rich") Yogurt Liqueur — a Japan Food Selection gold winner, unpasteurised and kept refrigerated. Strawberry and Zao-highland versions extend the line.

超濃厚ヨーグルト酒（ジャージー）.specs_en: Sake base, 100% Jersey yogurt — 5% ABV, keep refrigerated

miyazaki:unkai_shuzo.tagline_en: Hyuganatsu, kumquat and mango — Miyazaki's orchard in a shochu house's liqueurs.
miyazaki:unkai_shuzo.desc_en: Unkai Shuzo, the Miyazaki shochu maker, bottles the prefecture's fruit — hyuganatsu citrus, kumquat and mountain peach — as liqueurs, with a popular mango sparkling. Its Aya Shusen no Mori estate is open for visits and shopping.
features_en: Visitable Aya Shusen no Mori estate

miyazaki:inoue_shuzo_miyazaki.tagline_en: Hyuga no Natsuko — local citrus resting in the Obisugi barley shochu.
miyazaki:inoue_shuzo_miyazaki.desc_en: Inoue Shuzo of Nichinan, Miyazaki, known for the honkaku shochu Obisugi, steeps local hyuganatsu citrus in its barley shochu for Hyuga no Natsuko and other fruit liqueurs.

miyazaki:takachiho_shuzo.tagline_en: Oak-aged plum genshu and Meyer lemon from the shrine country of Takachiho.
miyazaki:takachiho_shuzo.desc_en: Takachiho Shuzo, a shochu house in Takachiho, Miyazaki, makes liqueurs from local materials: an oak-cask-aged plum genshu, a hyuganatsu mikan liqueur and a Meyer lemon liqueur.

miyazaki:sakuranosato.tagline_en: A limited strawberry liqueur from the house of 5,500 great clay pots.
miyazaki:sakuranosato.desc_en: Sakuranosato Shuzo, established in 1994 as a sister company of Inoue Shuzo, ages its spirits in about 5,500 large clay pots — among the most in Japan — and is known for the shochus Mugetsu and Aka-Mao. Its Shiawase strawberry liqueur is released in limited quantities at 14% ABV.
features_en: About 5,500 ageing pots — among Japan's largest

nagano:chikumanishiki.tagline_en: Saku's 1681 house, a silver medallist with its shochu-genshu umeshu.
nagano:chikumanishiki.desc_en: Chikumanishiki Shuzo, founded in 1681 in Saku, Nagano, brews with spring water of the Asama range and Nagano rice. Its Gokujo Genshu UMESHU took silver in the honkaku-shochu division of the 2024 National Umeshu Awards.
features_en: Silver, honkaku-shochu division, 2024 National Umeshu Awards

nagano:kikuisuishuzo_nagano.tagline_en: The only brewery of the Iida valley, from sake to cider.
nagano:kikuisuishuzo_nagano.desc_en: Kikuisui Shuzo is the only brewery in the Iida–Shimoina area of southern Nagano, making sake alongside shochu, liqueurs and cider in the Shinshu countryside.

nagasaki:ikinokura.tagline_en: Umeshu from Iki, the island where barley shochu was born.
nagasaki:ikinokura.desc_en: Ikinokura Shuzo was formed in 1984 when six distillers on Iki Island joined forces. Keeping the island's 16th-century shochu tradition, it also makes an umeshu on its barley shochu base.

nagasaki:fukuda_shuzo.tagline_en: The westernmost brewery on Japan's main islands, ranging from sake to gin.
nagasaki:fukuda_shuzo.desc_en: Fukuda Shuzo, founded in 1688 in Hirado, is the westernmost brewery on Japan's main islands and served the Hirado domain. One of Nagasaki's most capable houses, it makes sake, shochu, liqueurs, gin and amazake.
features_en: Founded 1688 — westernmost on the main islands

nara:umenoyado.tagline_en: The Aragoshi house — fruit flesh left whole, from a Nara brewery of 1893.
nara:umenoyado.desc_en: Umenoyado, founded in 1893 in Katsuragi, Nara, is best known for its Aragoshi series — sake-based liqueurs generous with whole fruit pulp: umeshu at 8% ABV, mikan, peach, yuzu and strawberry. The style is mellow and thick with fruit.
features_en: Aragoshi series with whole fruit pulp

あらごし梅酒.specs_en: Sake base with plum pulp — 8% ABV

nara:narakasugayama.tagline_en: The Hanafuda umeshu, a long-seller since 2003 from the springs below Kasuga's primeval forest.
nara:narakasugayama.desc_en: Nara Kasugayama Shuzo — founded in 1877 and renamed from Yagi Shuzo in 2022 — sits on famous spring water at the foot of the Kasuga primeval forest. Its Hanafuda series of umeshu and yuzushu, launched in 2003, is a long-seller with many awards at home and abroad.

nara:kitaoka_honten.tagline_en: Yoshino Monogatari — liqueurs of homegrown fruit from the cherry-blossom mountain.
nara:kitaoka_honten.desc_en: Kitaoka Honten, founded in 1868 in Yoshino — Japan's most famous cherry-blossom country — carries the three-legged crow Yatagarasu on its label and makes the Yoshino Monogatari line: umeshu with local Yoshino plums, plus whole-fruit yuzu and peach liqueurs on shochu.
features_en: The Yatagarasu crow on its label

niigata:hakkaisan_liqueur.tagline_en: Hakkaisan's umeshu, mellowed in a snow-cooled cellar.
niigata:hakkaisan_liqueur.desc_en: Hakkaisan Brewery, founded in 1922 in Minamiuonuma, steeps domestic plums in its own honkaku rice shochu for an umeshu at 14% ABV, matured at low temperature in a yukimuro — a traditional snow-cooled cellar.

niigata:kikusui_niigata.tagline_en: Beni Kikusui — three Niigata plum varieties in junmai sake.
niigata:kikusui_niigata.desc_en: Kikusui, the Niigata brewery founded in 1881 in Shibata, makes Beni Kikusui, an umeshu of Niigata-grown Koshi-no-ume, Kosaka and Togoro plums steeped in its junmai sake.
features_en: Three Niigata plum varieties in junmai

niigata:yoshinogawa.tagline_en: A 1548 Nagaoka house, ageing Benisashi plums in sake since 2012.
niigata:yoshinogawa.desc_en: Yoshinogawa, founded in 1548 in Nagaoka and among Japan's oldest breweries, steeps Fukui-grown Benisashi plums in sake for its Gensen Umeshu, an amber liqueur it has aged since 2012.

oita:oyama_yumekobo.tagline_en: An umeshu-only house in Oyama plum country, built with Nikka Whisky.
oita:oyama_yumekobo.desc_en: Oyama Yumekobo in Hita, Oita, is a dedicated umeshu maker whose plant was built together with Nikka Whisky. It uses only plums grown by farmers of the local Oyama district and has taken gold at the National Umeshu Awards two years running; in 2024 its The FIRST and an Earl Grey tea-blend umeshu both took silver.
features_en: Dedicated umeshu maker with a Nikka-built plant
Two straight National Umeshu Awards golds

和紅茶梅酒 アールグレイエモーショナル.name_en: Japanese Black Tea Umeshu "Earl Grey Emotional"

oita:oimatsu.tagline_en: Tenku no Tsuki — a yuzu umeshu from Hita's 1789 house.
oita:oimatsu.desc_en: Oimatsu Shuzo, founded in 1789 in Hita, Oita, makes the Tenku no Tsuki line; its yuzu umeshu won silver in the citrus-blend division of the 2024 National Umeshu Awards.

oita:kuge_honten.desc_en: Kuge Honten of Usuki, Oita, makes Iyanbai Umeshu on a honkaku shochu base; it won silver in the honkaku-shochu division of the 2024 National Umeshu Awards.

oita:yatsushika.tagline_en: coconoe — a barley-shochu yogurt liqueur with a grown-up bitter edge.
oita:yatsushika.desc_en: Yatsushika Shuzo of Kokonoe, Oita, blends Kyushu yogurt into its own honkaku barley shochu for coconoe, a yogurt liqueur at 8% ABV with a faint shochu bitterness. It placed third in the liqueur division of the Tenma Tenjin Umeshu Festival.
features_en: Third place, Tenma Tenjin liqueur division

八鹿 coconoe（ここのえ）.specs_en: Barley shochu base, Kyushu yogurt — 8% ABV

okayama:miyashita_shuzo.tagline_en: Okayama's everything-house — Gokujo sake, Doppo beer, and an umeshu besides.
okayama:miyashita_shuzo.desc_en: Miyashita Shuzo, a composite drinks maker with a century of history in Okayama, brews the sake Gokujo and the craft beer Doppo, and makes umeshu, gin and whisky besides.
features_en: Sake, beer, umeshu, gin and whisky

okayama:tsuji_honten.tagline_en: Gozenshu umeshu — Maniwa plums, sake, and nothing added at all.
okayama:tsuji_honten.desc_en: Tsuji Honten, founded in 1804 in Katsuyama, Okayama, makes a completely additive-free umeshu of local Maniwa plums on its Gozenshu sake — a clean, dry-leaning pour — with a yuzushu alongside.

okinawa:seifuku.tagline_en: Ishigaki's awamori umeshu, with shikuwasa from the islands.
okinawa:seifuku.desc_en: Seifuku Shuzo, the Ishigaki Island awamori distillery founded in 1949, makes a rich awamori-based umeshu at 12% ABV and a shikuwasa citrus liqueur from Okinawan fruit — southern-island liqueurs with real character.

okinawa:zuisen.tagline_en: Shuri's awamori house, sweetening its umeshu with Okinawan black sugar.
okinawa:zuisen.desc_en: Zuisen Shuzo, founded in 1887 in Shuri, Naha, makes Zuisen Umeshu on awamori, sweetened with Okinawan black sugar and made with Wakayama plums — 12% ABV.
features_en: Okinawan black sugar in the umeshu

瑞泉梅酒.specs_en: Awamori base, Okinawan black sugar — 12% ABV

okinawa:kumesen.tagline_en: 100% Okinawan shikuwasa on awamori, with nothing added.
okinawa:kumesen.desc_en: Kumesen Shuzo, one of Okinawa's leading awamori makers, presses a shikuwasa liqueur from 100% Okinawan shikuwasa juice on its awamori — 7% ABV, free of flavourings, colourings and preservatives.

okinawa:chukou.tagline_en: Umeshu built on kusu — Okinawa's aged awamori.
okinawa:chukou.desc_en: Chukou Shuzo of Tomigusuku, Okinawa, steeps its umeshu in kusu — aged awamori — for the Kusu Umeshu at 12% ABV.

osaka:choya.tagline_en: The name the world knows for umeshu — whole Nanko plums, exported to 40 countries.
osaka:choya.desc_en: Choya, founded in 1914 in Habikino, Osaka, is Japan's defining umeshu maker. It steeps whole Nanko plums in its authentic method and ships The CHOYA and its other lines to more than forty countries — the name most drinkers abroad first meet umeshu through.

The CHOYA AGED 3 YEARS.specs_en: Three years aged, Nanko plums — 17% ABV

osaka:suntory_liqueur.tagline_en: Kanade's four seasons and Midori's world stage — Japan in a bartender's bottle.
osaka:suntory_liqueur.desc_en: Suntory's liqueur portfolio expresses the Japanese seasons in the Kanade series — sakura, matcha, white peach and yuzu, all at 25% ABV and poured in bars worldwide as cocktail bases. Midori, its melon liqueur launched in 1978 with Shizuoka muskmelon among its fruit, is sold in more than fifty countries.
features_en: Cocktail bases used in bars worldwide
Midori — a global melon liqueur since 1978

ミドリ MIDORI メロンリキュール.specs_en: Shizuoka muskmelon — 23% ABV, sold in 50+ countries since 1978

osaka:kawachi_wine.tagline_en: Ebisu Fukuume — a winery's umeshu deepened with 20-year-aged reserves.
osaka:kawachi_wine.desc_en: Kawachi Wine, the winery of Osaka's Kawachi district, makes brandy-based umeshu. Its Ebisu Fukuume blends in umeshu aged twenty years for a secret depth, balancing sweetness against acidity.

saga:amabuki.tagline_en: Flower-yeast brewers whose daiginjo umeshu wears National Umeshu Awards gold.
saga:amabuki.desc_en: Amabuki Shuzo, founded in the Genroku era (1688–1704) in Miyaki, Saga, is famed for brewing sake with flower yeasts. Its Ryuo umeshu, steeped in daiginjo sake, holds National Umeshu Awards gold, and its tete Aromatics Japan Botanicals took gold in the blend division in 2024.
features_en: Gold at the National Umeshu Awards

天吹梅酒 龍王 大吟醸仕込.specs_en: Daiginjo base — National Umeshu Awards laureate

saga:mitsutake.tagline_en: From the Makai e no Izanai house — a healing nigori umeshu.
saga:mitsutake.desc_en: Mitsutake Shuzojo of Kashima, Saga, known for the imo shochu Makai e no Izanai ("Invitation to the Demon World"), makes Iyashi no Umeshu, a cloudy umeshu that won silver in the nigori division of the 2024 National Umeshu Awards.
features_en: The Makai e no Izanai shochu house

saitama:asahara.tagline_en: An umeshu on Cabernet Sauvignon — Saitama plums meet red wine.
saitama:asahara.desc_en: Asahara Shuzo of Moroyama, which brews Saitama sake, beer and wine, makes an unusual umeshu of local plums steeped on a red-wine base of Cabernet Sauvignon.
features_en: Sake, beer and wine under one roof

saitama:kingshop_makotoya.tagline_en: Tsurugashima's rain-prayer umeshu, a silver medallist in 2024.
saitama:kingshop_makotoya.desc_en: Kingshop Makotoya of Tsurugashima, Saitama, makes the Amagoi ("rain prayer") Umeshu II, which won silver in the blend division of the 2024 National Umeshu Awards.
features_en: Silver, blend division, 2024 National Umeshu Awards

shiga:kitajima.tagline_en: Miyonosakae umeshu from a 1805 Shiga house.
shiga:kitajima.desc_en: Kitajima Shuzo, founded in 1805 in Konan, Shiga, brews the Miyonosakae sake line and a sake-based umeshu of domestic plums.

shiga:ota_shuzo_shiga.tagline_en: Descendants of the castle-builder Dokan, pouring sake, wine and liqueur.
shiga:ota_shuzo_shiga.desc_en: Ota Shuzo of Kusatsu, Shiga, traces its line to Ota Dokan, builder of Edo Castle. Alongside its sake Dokan it makes wine and brandy from 100% Japanese grapes and a range of fruit liqueurs.
features_en: Descended from Ota Dokan, builder of Edo Castle

shimane:ichinomiya.tagline_en: By the silver-mine World Heritage — yuzu, apple, even a rose liqueur.
shimane:ichinomiya.desc_en: Ichinomiya Shuzo, with more than 120 years of history in Oda, Shimane — home of the Iwami Ginzan World Heritage silver mine — makes a wide liqueur range: umeshu, yuzu, apple and even a rose liqueur.

shimane:yoshida_shuzo_shimane.tagline_en: Gassan Ume-sake, from the old house at the foot of the mountain.
shimane:yoshida_shuzo_shimane.desc_en: Yoshida Shuzo, founded in 1743 at the foot of Mt. Gassan in Yasugi, Shimane, brews the sake Gassan and makes the sake-based Gassan Ume-sake plum liqueur.

shizuoka:hananomai.tagline_en: An additive-free junmai umeshu that took second in all Japan.
shizuoka:hananomai.desc_en: Hananomai, the Hamamatsu brewery that works only with Shizuoka-grown rice, steeps fine Nanko plums in its sake for an additive-free umeshu that placed second at the 3rd National Umeshu Awards in 2017.

花の舞 純米梅酒.specs_en: Sake base, Nanko plums, additive-free — 2nd, National Umeshu Awards

shizuoka:fujimasa_shuzo.tagline_en: Watashi no Umeshu — pesticide-free green plums at the closest brewery to Mt. Fuji.
shizuoka:fujimasa_shuzo.desc_en: Fujimasa Shuzo, founded in 1866 and the brewery nearest Mt. Fuji since moving to the Asagiri highlands (900 m) in 2011, makes Watashi no Umeshu from local pesticide-free green plums of Fujinomiya steeped in undiluted sake.
features_en: The closest brewery to Mt. Fuji
Local pesticide-free green plums in sake genshu

ワタシの梅酒.specs_en: Sake genshu base, pesticide-free Fujinomiya plums

tochigi:shimazaki.tagline_en: Cave-ageing specialists with a local-plum umeshu and a Tochiotome strawberry wine.
tochigi:shimazaki.desc_en: Shimazaki Shuzo, founded in 1849 in Nasukarasuyama and known for long ageing in its cave cellars, steeps local green plums in sake for Azuma Rikishi Umeshu and makes a strawberry wine of 100% Tochiotome berries, free of flavourings and colourings.
features_en: Local plums and 100% Tochiotome strawberry wine

tochigi:tonoike.tagline_en: Mashiko Tochiotome berries, jam-sweet in the glass.
tochigi:tonoike.desc_en: Tonoike Shuzoten of Mashiko, Tochigi, makes Ichigo no Osake from locally grown Tochiotome strawberries — jam-like in aroma at 12% ABV — and a peach liqueur blended with its sake Nozomu.
features_en: Peach liqueur blended with Nozomu sake

tochigi:kobayashi_shuzo.tagline_en: Hoo Biden's patent trick — whole peaches liquefied, cell by cell.
tochigi:kobayashi_shuzo.desc_en: Kobayashi Shuzo, founded in 1872 in Oyama and nationally famous for the ginjo sake Hoo Biden, uses its own patented technique to break peaches down cell by cell into liquid — the Kanjuku Momo, a luxuriously pulpy liqueur on a ginjo base at 5–6% ABV, refrigerated with a three-month shelf life. A Tochiotome strawberry version follows.

tochigi:nishibori_shuzo.tagline_en: I MY ME — ancient red and green rice sake beneath pure Tochiotome juice.
tochigi:nishibori_shuzo.desc_en: Nishibori Shuzo, founded in 1872 in Oyama with cellars on the national tangible cultural property register, makes the Aimaimi "I MY ME" strawberry liqueur — 100% straight Tochiotome juice from Tochigi on a junmai base brewed from ancient red and green rice.

tokushima:honke_matsuura.tagline_en: Sudachi-shu from Tokushima's oldest brewery — thirty years a favourite.
tokushima:honke_matsuura.desc_en: Honke Matsuura, founded in 1804 and the oldest surviving brewery in Tokushima, brews Naruto Tai sake and blends Tokushima's own sudachi citrus juice with honey and sake for its Shumurie Sudachi-shu — a long-seller of more than thirty years.

しゅムリエ すだち酒.specs_en: Sake base, Tokushima sudachi and honey

tokushima:awaglass.tagline_en: Wasanbon sugar in the umeshu — gold in Japan's first umeshu special zone.
tokushima:awaglass.desc_en: Awaglass, established in 2010 in the Misato district — Japan's first umeshu special production zone — sweetens its plum liqueur with Tokushima's traditional wasanbon sugar. Its Wasanbon Umeshu won gold in the mixed-base division of the 2024 National Umeshu Awards.
features_en: In Japan's first umeshu special zone

tokushima:higashino_liqueur.tagline_en: Licence No. 1 of the umeshu zone — a couple's tiny kura and its warbler-named star.
tokushima:higashino_liqueur.desc_en: Higashino Liqueur holds licence No. 1 (2008) of the Misato umeshu special zone — a small kura run by a couple who returned from Kyoto. Their Hohokekyo, named for the warbler's song, is a certified Tokushima Premium Brand (2016) and took silver in the white-liquor division of the 2024 National Umeshu Awards. Dry, shiso-tinted and rich styles round out the range.

ホーホケキョ.specs_en: 12% ABV, fruity — Tokushima Premium Brand; silver, 2024

tokushima:oobatake.tagline_en: Nothing added, nothing dressed up — plums into the jar within 24 hours of picking.
tokushima:oobatake.desc_en: Oobatake, in full production since 2011 in the Misato umeshu zone, pursues umeshu as bare genshu — no dilution, no additives — steeping Misato plums within twenty-four hours of harvest. The long-aged Hotaru no Yado reaches 21% ABV.
features_en: Plums steeped within 24 hours of picking

tokushima:tokunaga_umeshu.tagline_en: TOKAMI — a rich brandy umeshu of Oshuku and Gessekai plums.
tokushima:tokunaga_umeshu.desc_en: Tokunaga Umeshu, a young couple's kura in Misato, makes TOKAMI, its signature brandy-based aged umeshu at 18% ABV, from two local plum varieties — Oshuku and Gessekai — with rock sugar.

TOKAMI.specs_en: Brandy base, Oshuku and Gessekai plums — 18% ABV

tokushima:fuji_nogyo.tagline_en: Three plums, three characters — farmers ageing each variety three years.
tokushima:fuji_nogyo.desc_en: The Fuji agricultural cooperative, run by Misato farmers, ages its umeshu three years in the traditional way, drawing flavour to the very kernel. Three plum varieties — Ryukyo, Oshuku and Gessekai — are each bottled separately to show their character. The co-op also runs the Misato umeshu festival.

tokyo:ishikawa_shuzo.tagline_en: Tama no Yaeume — Tokyo umeshu, hand-steeped at a 1863 Fussa kura.
tokyo:ishikawa_shuzo.desc_en: Ishikawa Shuzo, founded in 1863 in Fussa, Tokyo, has its craftsmen steep 100% Japanese plums for Tama no Yaeume — an umeshu of refined sweetness and plum fragrance.

tokyo:ozawa_shuzo.tagline_en: Sawanoi's Purari — umeshu from the clear-stream brewery of Okutama.
tokyo:ozawa_shuzo.desc_en: Ozawa Shuzo, founded in 1702 by the clear streams of Okutama in western Tokyo, brews the famous Sawanoi sake and makes the Sawanoi Umeshu Purari.

tokyo:koh_inc.tagline_en: Soteinai — "as expected" — a double-medal premium umeshu.
tokyo:koh_inc.desc_en: Koh Inc. makes the Soteinai ("as expected") umeshu series, which took both gold and silver in the premium division of the 2024 National Umeshu Awards for its 2022 and 2021 vintages.
features_en: Gold and silver, premium division, 2024 National Umeshu Awards

tokyo:godo_shusei.tagline_en: Oshukubai Gokujo — a brandy-blend umeshu from the Oenon group.
tokyo:godo_shusei.desc_en: Godo Shusei, part of the Oenon group, makes the Honkaku Umeshu Oshukubai Gokujo — silver in the brandy-blend division of the 2024 National Umeshu Awards — and the Kajitsu no Rakuen fruit series.

tottori:chiyomusubi.tagline_en: Sakaiminato's playful house — from GeGeGe collab umeshu to the ULTRA fruit line.
tottori:chiyomusubi.desc_en: Chiyomusubi Shuzo, founded in 1865 in Sakaiminato, Tottori, ranges wide: umeshu including a GeGeGe no Kitaro collaboration bottle, and the ULTRA series of peach, yuzu and mango liqueurs.

tottori:inata_honten.tagline_en: A 1673 Yonago house of rice, water and people — liqueurs included.
tottori:inata_honten.desc_en: Inata Honten, founded in 1673 in Yonago, Tottori, brews with devotion to people, rice and water, and extends its craft into liqueurs.

toyama:wakatsuru.tagline_en: UMESKY — plums steeped in the house's own whisky.
toyama:wakatsuru.desc_en: Wakatsuru Shuzo, founded in 1862 in Tonami, Toyama, makes sake, shochu and whisky — the last at its Saburomaru distillery — and steeps plums in its own whisky for UMESKY, a serious umeshu with a whisky backbone.
features_en: Umeshu on the house's own whisky
Saburomaru distillery under the same roof

toyama:tamaasahi.tagline_en: Soft Tateyama water and fruity experiments in the Owara dance town of Yatsuo.
toyama:tamaasahi.desc_en: Tamaasahi Shuzo, founded in 1808 in Yatsuo — the Toyama town famous for the Owara Kaze no Bon festival — brews with soft underground water of the Joganji river system fed by the Tateyama range, and has turned in recent years to sweet, fruity liqueurs.
features_en: Founded 1808 in the Owara festival town

wakayama:nakano_bc.tagline_en: An umeshu specialist in the Nanko plum homeland — green-tea umeshu included.
wakayama:nakano_bc.desc_en: Nakano BC, founded in 1932 in Kainan, Wakayama — the homeland of the Kishu Nanko plum — is a dedicated umeshu maker with a long list of awards. The Kishu line spans a honey umeshu, a green-tea umeshu and the brandy-steeped Fujishiro Muku at 19% ABV.
features_en: Umeshu specialist in Nanko plum country

wakayama:godaian.tagline_en: Genshu umeshu gold from the plum farms of Minabe.
wakayama:godaian.desc_en: Godaian of Minabe, Wakayama, makes umeboshi and umeshu from Nanko plums at their source. Its Genshu Umeshu won gold in the white-liquor division of the 2024 National Umeshu Awards; a brandy-blend Shoya Zenpachi follows.
features_en: Made at the source of Nanko plums

wakayama:nakata_foods.tagline_en: Wakayama's plum-product standard-bearer, with a citrus-blend medallist.
wakayama:nakata_foods.desc_en: Nakata Foods of Tanabe, Wakayama, is one of the prefecture's defining umeboshi and umeshu makers, working with Kishu Nanko plums. Its citrus-blend Runrun Mikan Umeshu took silver at the 2024 National Umeshu Awards.

wakayama:plum_foods.tagline_en: Cask-finished ripe-plum umeshu, with a distillery of its own since 2019.
wakayama:plum_foods.desc_en: Plum Foods, founded in 1969 in Minabe, makes liqueurs, drinks and jams from Kishu Nanko plums, and opened the Kishu Kumano Distillery in 2019 to add distilled spirits. Its cask-aged fully-ripe plum umeshu leads the line.

wakayama:shokibai.tagline_en: SHOKIBAI — brandy-blend gold at the 2024 National Umeshu Awards.
wakayama:shokibai.desc_en: Shokibai of Minabe, Wakayama, makes the Honkaku Umeshu SHOKIBAI from Kishu Nanko plums; it won gold in the brandy-blend division of the 2024 National Umeshu Awards.

wakayama:maruryo_nagaoka.tagline_en: Kishu Moe, a white-liquor silver medallist from Nanko country.
wakayama:maruryo_nagaoka.desc_en: Maruryo Nagaoka makes Kishu Moe from Kishu Nanko plums; it won silver in the white-liquor division of the 2024 National Umeshu Awards.

yamagata:dewazakura.tagline_en: The ginjo pioneers, brewing a sake purely to become umeshu.
yamagata:dewazakura.desc_en: Dewazakura, the Tendo brewery founded in 1892 that pioneered ginjo sake for everyday drinkers, brews a dedicated junmai sake purely for steeping plums. Three styles — tart-dry, ripe and pulpy nigori — each took silver at the 2024 National Umeshu Awards, and the Torokeru Yamagata line bottles local peach and grape on a ginjo base.
features_en: A junmai brewed solely for umeshu
Three silvers at the 2024 National Umeshu Awards

出羽桜 とろけるやまがた もも.specs_en: Yamagata peach, 90%+ juice, ginjo base — 8% ABV

yamagata:tatenokawa.tagline_en: Kodakara — Japan's first local-yogurt liqueur, and its best-selling one.
yamagata:tatenokawa.desc_en: Tatenokawa, founded in 1832 in Sakata, created Japan's first local-yogurt liqueur — Kodakara Chokai Sanroku Yogurt — and leads the category in sales. Raw-milk yogurt from dairies at the foot of Mt. Chokai makes up over 60% of the bottle, on a sake base at 8% ABV; an unpasteurised nama-toro version is kept refrigerated.

yamagata:wada_shuzo.tagline_en: Nomanega Kahoku — "won't you have a drink?" in Yamagata dialect.
yamagata:wada_shuzo.desc_en: Wada Shuzo, founded in 1797 in Kahoku and brewer of the sake Aradama, blends yogurt from the local Osei dairy with its sake for Nomanega Kahoku — the name is Yamagata dialect for "won't you have a drink?". Kept refrigerated.

Nomanega Kahoku（のまねが かほく）.specs_en: Sake base, Kahoku yogurt — keep refrigerated

yamaguchi:dassai.tagline_en: Umeshu steeped in Dassai 23 — the world's best-known junmai daiginjo.
yamaguchi:dassai.desc_en: Asahi Shuzo of Iwakuni, Yamaguchi — the house of Dassai — steeps plums in its junmai daiginjo for the Dassai Migaki Niwari-sanbu Umeshu, a luxurious plum liqueur built on rice polished to 23%.

yamaguchi:okazaki_shuzojo.tagline_en: Hagi yuzu and natsumikan on sake, from the waters of the Chomonkyo gorge.
yamaguchi:okazaki_shuzojo.desc_en: Okazaki Shuzojo of Hagi, Yamaguchi, brews with subsoil water of the Abu River flowing through the Chomonkyo gorge, and makes popular sake-based liqueurs of Hagi's own yuzu and natsumikan citrus.

yamanashi:sasaichi.tagline_en: A 1661 Otsuki house on Mt. Fuji's underground water, umeshu included.
yamanashi:sasaichi.desc_en: Sasaichi Shuzo, founded in 1661 in Otsuki, Yamanashi, brews with the subsoil water of Mt. Fuji and makes umeshu and other liqueurs alongside its sake.
